paragraphs.sourceText: You might think of your teeth as tools, like built-in knives and forks, but if they are mere tools, why do they feel pain and wouldn't it be better if they could just 26 under any condition? In spite of our 27 discomfort, it turns out there's a good reason our teeth are so sensitive. Tooth pain is a 28 mechanism that ensures when a tooth is being damaged we'll notice and do something about it.

If we eat something too hot or too cold, or if the tooth is worn down enough where the tissue 29 is exposed, all of those things cause pain, and then the pain causes the person not to use that tooth to try to protect it a little bit more. So it's really a protective mechanism more than anything else. If teeth didn't feel pain, we might 30 to use them in situations that damage them, and for humans, damaging 31 teeth is a problem because, unlike crocodiles, we can't 32 them.

Teeth have three layers, only one of which-the innermost layer of the tooth-can hurt, as that layer of the tooth 33 both blood vessels and nerves. Pain is the only feeling to which the nerves in that layer respond. Whereas people with tooth sensitivity may complain, for example, of tooth pain 34 by heat or cold, the nerves in the inner layer don't sense temperature. Rather, they feel pain, which may be 35 with, say, drinking something very cold.

paragraphs.sourceText: How to determine if a company is a good fit for you
paragraphs.translationZh: 如何判断一家公司是否适合你

paragraphs.sourceText: A) On paper, the job seemed perfect for me: The position was completely in line with my degree, the duties and responsibilities were compatible with my interests, and the office maintained a well-stocked kitchen that would satisfy my every snack desire.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 从表面上看，这份工作对我来说似乎很完美：这个职位完全符合我的学位，职责和责任符合我的兴趣，办公室有一个储备充足的厨房，可以满足我对零食的所有渴望。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) Sounds like my dream job, right? There was only one small problem: I simply didn't get along with the company culture. They favored a more rigid, closed-door, corporate atmosphere, while I would have preferred something more collaborative and open. They were complete clock watchers, while I would have liked a more flexible schedule. To put it plainly, we just weren,t on the same page.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 听起来像是我梦想的工作，对吧？只有一个小问题：我根本不适应公司文化。他们喜欢更严格、更封闭的企业氛围，而我则更喜欢更具协作性和开放性的氛围。他们是十足的时钟观察者，而我则希望有更灵活的时间表。说白了，我们只是意见不一致。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) When it comes to looking for a new job, you already know that a big part of the interview process involves the company evaluating whether or not you're a good fit for their open role. But, it's important to keep in mind that the employer isn't the only one who needs to identify a good match- you should be looking for that same exact thing. Company culture can have a big impact on how you feel about your work, so you want to make sure you sign an offer letter with an organization you're truly excited about.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 在寻找新工作时，您已经知道面试过程的很大一部分涉及公司评估您是否适合他们的空缺职位。但是，重要的是要记住，雇主并不是唯一需要确定良好匹配的人 - 您应该寻找同样的东西。公司文化会对您对工作的感受产生重大影响，因此您需要确保与您真正感兴趣的组织签署录用通知书。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) However, figuring out what a company is like before you actually work there can be a bit of a challenge. Luckily, there are a few things you can do to determine whether or not a company is a good fit for you- before you ever sign your name on that dotted line.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 然而，在你真正工作之前弄清楚一家公司是什么样的可能会有点挑战。幸运的是，在您在那条虚线上签名之前，您可以采取一些措施来确定一家公司是否适合您。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) First of all, know what you want. It's hard to make any decisions when you don't really know what you're looking for. So before you can determine whether you and a specific company would be compatible together, it's important to have a solid handle on what exactly you want from your employer. Many of us have an easier time identifying the things that we absolutely don't want. If those are the only things you can think of, don't worry! That's still a good place to start.
paragraphs.translationZh: E）首先，知道你想要什么。当您不真正知道自己在寻找什么时，很难做出任何决定。因此，在确定您和特定公司是否兼容之前，重要的是要充分了解您到底想从雇主那里得到什么。我们中的许多人可以更容易地识别出我们绝对不想要的东西。如果这些是您唯一能想到的，别担心！这仍然是一个很好的起点。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Start by writing down the things you didn't like about previous employers, as well as the parts you really valued. There 9s no wrong answer here一so from big things to small details, write them all down on your list. This will help you immediately identify what you're looking for in an organization, as well as the things you're trying to stay far, far away from.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 首先写下你不喜欢前雇主的地方，以及你真正看重的部分。这里没有 9 个错误的答案——所以从大事到小细节，把它们都写在你的清单上。这将帮助你立即确定你在组织中寻找什么，以及你试图远离什么。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Make sure to do your research. Now comes the part when you put on your detective hat and do a little digging. The Internet will be your best friend when you're trying to familiarize yourself with a company's culture before ever walking through their office doors. And where exactly should you look for these culture clues? Start with the most obvious place first: the company's website. Read through their copy and blog. Do they use formal, direct language? Or is it casual, conversational, and maybe even a little humorous? This can be a big indicator of what sort of atmosphere the company is trying to cultivate.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 确保做好研究。现在是你戴上侦探帽并进行一些挖掘的部分。当您在走进公司办公室门之前尝试熟悉公司文化时，互联网将是您最好的朋友。您究竟应该在哪里寻找这些文化线索？首先从最明显的地方开始：公司网站。通读他们的副本和博客。他们使用正式、直接的语言吗？或者是随意的、对话式的，甚至可能有点幽默？这可以作为公司正在努力营造什么样的氛围的一个重要指标。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Next, turn your attention toward their social media outlets. Are they sharing photos of their team's Thursday afternoon barbeque or Halloween costume contest? Or are their social media accounts strictly reserved for company-related announcements and product launches?
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 接下来，将注意力转向他们的社交媒体渠道。他们是否分享了他们的团队周四下午烧烤或万圣节服装比赛的照片？或者他们的社交媒体帐户是否严格保留用于公司相关公告和产品发布？

paragraphs.sourceText: I) An industry review website like Glassdoor is another spot to check in order to find some insider information about what you can expect about a company. However, remember to take the reviews you read with a grain of salt-many of them are written by scorned (被啬口视的)employees.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 像 Glassdoor 这样的行业评论网站是另一个值得检查的地方，以便找到一些关于您对一家公司的期望的内幕信息。然而，请记住对你读到的评论持保留态度——其中许多评论是由被鄙视的员工写的。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Finally, you can never fail with personal connections. Send a quick message to a current or previous company employee on Linkedln or by email and ask if they would be willing to have a quick conversation with you about the organization in general. If you get a yes to your request for a chat, you911 be armed with some pretty powerful and helpful information heading into your interview!
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 最后，人际关系永远不会失败。通过 Linkedln 或电子邮件向现任或前任公司员工发送一条简短消息，询问他们是否愿意与您就公司的总体情况进行快速对话。如果您的聊天请求得到同意，您在面试时就会获得一些非常强大且有用的信息！

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Learn more by asking questions. You know that part at the end of a job interview when the hiring manager asks if you have any questions, and you just stare across the table blankly with your mouth hanging open? That's the perfect opportunity to speak up and get your burning company culture questions answered! So yes, you can definitely ask your interviewer about what it's like to work for that particular organization. Simple questions like, “What three words would you use to describe the culture here?” or “What's your favorite part about working for this company?can reveal a lot about what it's really like behind closed doors.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 通过提问了解更多信息。你知道面试结束时招聘经理问你是否有任何问题，而你只是张着嘴茫然地盯着桌子对面的那部分？这是畅所欲言并回答您紧迫的公司文化问题的绝佳机会！所以，是的，你绝对可以向面试官询问在该特定组织工作的感觉。简单的问题，例如“您会用哪三个词来形容这里的文化？”或“在这家公司工作你最喜欢的部分是什么？”可以揭示很多关于公司闭门工作的真实情况。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Prioritize your values. What does my dream company culture look like? Well, I could come and go as I please, as long as I was getting the work done. My boss would genuinely listen to and value all of my ideas arid suggestions. My co-workers would all be friendly with one another, without ever falling into the office gossip trap. The kitchen would have endless options of pizza and cookies. Oh, and they'd give me two months of paid vacation with a very generous salary.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 优先考虑你的价值观。我梦想的公司文化是什么样的？好吧，只要我能完成工作，我就可以随意来去。我的老板会真诚地倾听并重视我的所有想法和建议。我的同事们都会彼此友好，而不会陷入办公室八卦的陷阱。厨房里有无数的披萨和饼干可供选择。哦，他们会给我两个月的带薪假期和非常丰厚的薪水。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) What are my chances of finding all of those things with one employer? Slim to none— believe me, I've looked. This is why it's so important to know which aspects of a company's culture you value most. Is it an open communication style or a flexible schedule? Focus on the top spots on your priority list, and ensure a potential employer at least checks those boxes. Unfortunately, this is reality, you can,t have everything you want but a few are certainly achievable.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 我在一个雇主那里找到所有这些东西的机会有多大？几乎没有——相信我，我已经看过了。这就是为什么了解您最看重公司文化的哪些方面如此重要。是开放的沟通方式还是灵活的时间表？专注于你的优先列表中的首要位置，并确保潜在雇主至少选中这些框。不幸的是，这就是现实，你不可能拥有你想要的一切，但有一些肯定是可以实现的。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) When you're hunting for a new job, you already know that the employer is trying to decide whether or not you're a good fit for the position. But you should also look at the process through a similar lens. You may not be the one conducting the actual interview, but you're still trying to determine whether or not the company is a good fit for you.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 当您正在寻找新工作时，您已经知道雇主正在尝试确定您是否适合该职位。但您也应该通过类似的视角来看待这个过程。您可能不是进行实际面试的人，但您仍在尝试确定该公司是否适合您。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) Keep these tips in mind to figure out whether you and a potential employer are a perfect match or just a recipe (方案)for disaster. After all, it's a good thing to know before actually accepting an offer.
paragraphs.translationZh: O) 请记住这些提示，以了解您和潜在雇主是否是完美匹配，或者只是灾难的良方。毕竟，在真正接受报价之前了解一下是一件好事。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Clues about the culture of a company can be found on its website.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 有关公司文化的线索可以在其网站上找到。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. It can be difficult to know the real situation in a company until you become part of it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 在你成为公司的一部分之前，你可能很难了解公司的真实情况。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. It is impossible for a job applicant to have every expectation met.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 求职者的所有期望都不可能得到满足。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Simply by reading its description, the author found the job offered ideal.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 仅仅通过阅读其描述，作者就发现所提供的工作非常理想。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Job applicants are advised to make a written list of their likes and dislikes in their previous employment.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 建议求职者书面列出他们在之前工作中的喜好和厌恶。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. At the end of an interview, a job applicant should seize the opportunity to get answers to their urgent questions.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 面试结束时，求职者应该抓住机会获得紧急问题的答案。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. To begin with, job applicants should be clear what they expect from their future employer.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 首先，求职者应该清楚他们对未来雇主的期望。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Job applicants should read with a critical eye what is written about a company on the website.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 求职者应该以批判的眼光阅读网站上有关公司的文字。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Job satisfaction has a lot to do with company culture.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 工作满意度与公司文化有很大关系。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. A chat with an insider of a company can give job applicants very useful information when they prepare for an interview.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 当求职者准备面试时，与公司内部人士的聊天可以为他们提供非常有用的信息。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Online classes began to be popularized just a few decades ago. They are advertised as a way for adults to finish their education and students to learn the material at their own pace —it is far more compatible for people with busy schedules.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在线课程在几十年前才开始普及。它们被宣传为成人完成教育和学生按照自己的进度学习材料的一种方式——这对于日程繁忙的人来说更适合。

paragraphs.sourceText: But after being enrolled in an online course last fall semester, I came to realize online classes were merely a means to fulfil course requirements.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但去年秋季学期参加在线课程后，我开始意识到在线课程只是满足课程要求的一种手段。

paragraphs.sourceText: First of all, students lack the desire to learn, and they simply complete their assignments to receive credit for a passing grade rather than genuinely engage with the course material.
paragraphs.translationZh: 首先，学生缺乏学习的欲望，他们只是完成作业以获得及格分数的学分，而不是真正参与课程材料。

paragraphs.sourceText: As online courses tend to have more than 100 students, most of the assignments are short and simple. They are not designed for students to interact with the material in depth but designed to be graded easily to accommodate such a large number of students.
paragraphs.translationZh: 由于在线课程的学生人数往往超过 100 人，因此大多数作业都较短且简单。它们并不是为学生与材料进行深入互动而设计的，而是为了轻松评分以容纳如此多的学生而设计的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Perhaps the biggest disadvantage of taking an online class is the absence of face-to-face interaction between the teacher and their students. Live sessions are infrequent and are often scheduled during the middle of the day when students have to attend other classes or work. The office hours of the professor may also be during inconvenient times for many students as well. Most interaction with the professor has to be through email which is often impersonal. It is nearly impossible for students to build a relationship with their professor.
paragraphs.translationZh: 也许参加在线课程的最大缺点是老师和学生之间缺乏面对面的互动。现场课程并不频繁，通常安排在中午，当时学生必须参加其他课程或工作。教授的办公时间也可能是在许多学生不方便的时间。与教授的大多数互动必须通过电子邮件进行，这通常是非个人化的。学生几乎不可能与教授建立关系。

paragraphs.sourceText: There is also little interaction amongst students. It can be harder for students to create study groups and form relationships with their peers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 学生之间的互动也很少。对于学生来说，建立学习小组并与同龄人建立关系可能会更加困难。

paragraphs.sourceText: Online classes also require either a computer or laptop and a reliable internet connection. Not all students have access to these types of resources, whether it is for financial or other reasons, and some students can be put at a disadvantage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在线课程还需要计算机或笔记本电脑以及可靠的互联网连接。并非所有学生都能获得这些类型的资源，无论是出于经济原因还是其他原因，有些学生可能会处于不利地位。

paragraphs.sourceText: Offering online classes certainly helps students who would otherwise not be able to attend classroom sessions. However, they fail to provide a genuine education with an emphasis on convenience rather than critical thinking. We need restructured online classes in which students can have a learning experience that will actually provide quality education.
paragraphs.translationZh: 提供在线课程无疑可以帮助那些无法参加课堂课程的学生。然而，他们未能提供真正的教育，强调便利性而不是批判性思维。我们需要重组在线课程，让学生能够获得真正提供优质教育的学习体验。

paragraphs.sourceText: In the age of the internet, there's no such thing as a private debate. But is that bad for science? Some scientists have had concerns. When debates in any sector move beyond the halls of universities and government agencies, there's potential for information to be used incorrectly, leading to public confusion; yet, open debate can also promote communication between the scientific community and the public. Recent open debates on scientific research, health, and policy have aroused greater public attention and encouraged more diverse voices. If this trend spurs scientists to agree more quickly about the best solutions to our problems-and at the same time helps the public observe the process of scientific discourse more clearly- then this is good for everyone, including scientists.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在互联网时代，不存在私人辩论这样的事情。但这对科学有害吗？一些科学家对此表示担忧。当任何领域的辩论超出大学和政府机构的范围时，信息就有可能被错误使用，从而导致公众混乱；然而，公开辩论也可以促进科学界和公众之间的沟通。最近关于科学研究、健康和政策的公开辩论引起了公众更大的关注，并鼓励了更多不同的声音。如果这种趋势促使科学家更快地就解决我们问题的最佳解决方案达成一致，同时帮助公众更清楚地观察科学话语的过程，那么这对每个人都有好处，包括科学家。

paragraphs.sourceText: A recent debate published in The New York Times discussed the question of how quickly medicine should be developed and produced. Issues such as safety of the product and perception of the public were examined and considered. But some experts worried that such public speculation might lead people to believe that disagreement about the details meant a lack of adequate scientific consensus over the safety and efficiency of modern-day medicine.
paragraphs.translationZh: 《纽约时报》最近发表的一场辩论讨论了药物应以多快的速度开发和生产的问题。对产品安全性和公众认知等问题进行了审查和考虑。但一些专家担心，这种公众猜测可能会让人们相信，对细节的分歧意味着对现代医学的安全性和有效性缺乏足够的科学共识。

paragraphs.sourceText: The anxiety seems misplaced. Gone are the days of going to a conference and debating scientific issues, and that's good because those gatherings were not diverse enough and excluded many important voices. These days, the public can access debates about science regardless of where they take place.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种焦虑似乎用错了地方。参加会议和辩论科学问题的日子已经一去不复返了，这很好，因为这些聚会不够多元化，并且排除了许多重要的声音。如今，公众可以参与有关科学的辩论，无论辩论在哪里进行。

paragraphs.sourceText: For many scientists, public debate is a new frontier and it may feel like a place with few restraints or rules? but rather than avoiding such conversations, let the debates be transparent and vigorous, wherever they are held. If the public is to understand that science is an honorably self-correcting process, the idea that science is a fixed set of facts in a textbook needs to be dismissed. With the validity of science coming under attack, there's a need for scientific debates to be perceived as open and true to life. Let everyone see the noisy, messy deliberations that advance science and lead to decisions that benefit us all.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对于许多科学家来说，公共辩论是一个新领域，它可能感觉像是一个几乎没有限制或规则的地方？但与其避免此类对话，不如让辩论透明且激烈，无论在何处举行。如果公众要理解科学是一个光荣的自我纠正过程，那么就需要摒弃科学是教科书中一组固定事实的观点。随着科学的有效性受到攻击，科学辩论需要被认为是开放的、真实的。让每个人都看到那些喧闹、混乱的审议，这些审议推动了科学的发展并导致了造福于我们所有人的决策。
